title: Desert Hot Springs Police Recover $50,000 Stolen Generator Using Flock
body_markdown:
- Construction sites in Desert Hot Springs, California, are easy targets for theft. They often rely on temporary fencing and have no on-site security.
- A Flock license plate reader hotlist hit produced a picture of the truck towing the stolen trailer.
- Police identified the truck’s location, obtained a search warrant, made an arrest, and recovered all property before nightfall.


## **What Happened at the Desert Hot Springs Construction Site**


A generator worth about $50,000 was stolen from a construction site in Desert Hot Springs, California. No one witnessed the theft.


Desert Hot Springs has several active construction sites. According to Desert Hot Springs Police Department (DHSPD) Chief Steven Shaw, most don't have on-site security. Many use temporary fences, which are easy to get into and don't keep people out.


## **Why Construction Site Theft Is Hard to Solve**


The first officer on the scene looked for witnesses. The officer also checked for security cameras. There were none.


Without witnesses or footage, police had very little to go on. They did have one lead: a description of a truck.


## **How Flock Helped Identify the Suspect Vehicle**


DHSPD searched for the truck using Flock. The search returned a hit on the vehicle.


The hit included a picture of the truck towing the stolen trailer. That image tied the vehicle directly to the theft and gave officers a strong lead.


## **From Lead to Arrest in One Day**


Police moved quickly once they had the image. By the afternoon, they had identified the location. They also had a search warrant in hand.


The suspect was taken into custody. All of the stolen property was recovered before nightfall that day.


## **Getting the Crew Back to Work**


The construction company got its equipment back right away. The crew returned to work the next day. They used the recovered equipment to continue the job.


A fast recovery meant less lost time and less financial damage for the project.


## **Key Takeaway for Communities**


Even when a crime has no witnesses and no cameras at the scene, one small detail can be enough to crack the case. With Flock, the Desert Hot Springs Police Department turned a single vehicle description into a photo, a warrant, an arrest, and a full recovery in one day.
